tasks.short: Verify winnings and pay patrons or refer them to a cashier

steps.what: Receive the patron's ticket and identify the wager
Compute or read the settlement amount and verify winnings or losses
Pay the verified winnings directly to the patron
Refer the patron to the cashier when direct payout is unavailable
Record paid winnings or the cashier referral against the ticket

tasks.design: Configure a contextual settlement view and short outcome form in the {OTHER} wagering terminal. The writer verifies the amount, pays or refers the patron, and records the actual outcome; existing automatic settlement calculations earn no new saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding event and ticket context and repeating identifiers add transaction time.
tasks.enabler_now: Native ticket-context views and forms can shorten lookup and repeated identifiers.
tasks.still_hard: Disputed tickets, uncertain results and mismatched identity require human resolution.
tasks.human_edge: The writer checks the actual transaction and handles the patron fairly.
tasks.altitude: Small lookup and entry gains with unchanged payout responsibility.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of gambling services workers

evidence.claim: Native wagering-terminal context and forms can reduce navigation and repeated identifiers; existing automatic settlement is not new labour saving. The scenario is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes ticket receipt, computation or review, direct payment or referral and actual transaction recording. Payout and referral shares represent alternative case paths averaged across work.

The existing wagering terminal produces ticket id, event id, stake, odds, rule version and settlement status from the original wager; the authorised results feed supplies result and revision time. The writer retrieves and verifies provenance in s1 and s2; missing or provisional results stop payout for manual resolution.
The writer captures paid amount, ticket id, event id, outcome status and transaction time in s5. Entry and verification remain counted; no new structured capture is transferred to a cashier.

Test native settings first. The reduction in s2 is navigation only and in s5 repeated identifiers only. Actual calculation already done by the terminal, runtime and same-system saving receive no labour credit.
unknowns: Frequency of manual calculations and disputed tickets
research_questions: Does a native ticket view reduce navigation after all amount and status checks remain?

already_counted.description: Settlement verification, payment or referral checks and actual outcome entry remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain native view links and check settings after rule changes.

approvals.approved_version: Exact ticket, final result version, patron and cash amount checked immediately before s3 payout; any change voids the check.
Exact ticket, verified amount and internal cashier destination checked before s4 referral; changes require recheck.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R92.5, gross7.5 minus2 upkeep gives net5.5. Range0-3 assumes avoidable navigation and repeated identifiers, with calculation runtime and patron handling unchanged.

tasks.short: Pay off or move live bets according to game rules

steps.what: Read the applicable rules and current game outcome for live bets
Inspect the live bet positions and determine the required settlement
Pay off or move the live bets under the game procedure
Record the live-bet settlement and any procedural exception

tasks.design: Configure indexed house rules and a contextual live-bet log in the {OTHER} wagering system. The writer still inspects the actual bets, determines the action and physically pays or moves them, then records the outcome.
tasks.previous_blocker: Looking up the exact procedure and repeating game identifiers interrupt live settlement.
tasks.enabler_now: Native indexed rules and game-context forms can reduce those clerical fragments.
tasks.still_hard: Physical positions and disputed actions require immediate human attention.
tasks.human_edge: The writer sees the live state and applies the procedure in front of patrons.
tasks.altitude: No change in live-bet authority; less lookup and repeated logging.

reach.task: Apply a live game's settlement procedure
reach.learn: Physical bet-state verification and dispute handling

evidence.claim: Indexed rules and contextual live-bet logs can reduce navigation and repeated identifiers; no physical settlement automation or measured saving is claimed.

assumptions: This task covers live-bet movement or payoff at the game. Redeemed event-ticket payout is owned by task20596; the same transaction is not counted twice.

The authorised game operator produces the game outcome under the existing procedure; the writer observes it and checks the rule version in s1. Live bet positions are inspected in s2, not supplied as a free structured list.

The writer produces game id, outcome, action and exception text in s4 with capture time retained. Missing rule or uncertain outcome stops the action for manual resolution; no inferred bet state or automatic action is proposed.
Test native rule indexing and log settings first. Savings concern lookup and repeated identifiers, not same-system save or already automated settlement.
unknowns: Whether live-bet settlement occurs in this role's setting
research_questions: How much rule navigation and repeated game identification remains in live settlement?

already_counted.description: Inspection, actual settlement checks and record capture remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain current rule links and log context.

approvals.approved_version: Exact observed bet state, game outcome, rule version and intended payoff or movement checked before s3; a changed state voids the check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R92, gross8 minus2 upkeep gives net6. Range0-3 assumes avoidable rule lookup and repeated log identifiers; all live inspection and physical actions remain.

tasks.short: Record tickets cashed and payout amounts after each event

steps.what: Gather the cashed-ticket transactions for the completed race or event
Check which tickets were actually cashed and resolve missing entries
Count tickets cashed and total the event payout amounts
Re-enter event ticket counts and payouts in the separate event log
Review the event log against the checked transactions

tasks.design: First test the {OTHER} wagering system's native per-event report. Where staff still total an export and re-key a separate {SPREADSHEET} log, use native formulas and linked report cells for those two steps; transaction capture, reconciliation and review remain counted.
tasks.previous_blocker: An event log may repeat arithmetic and values already present in settled-ticket records.
tasks.enabler_now: Native reporting or a linked workbook can calculate totals and populate the recurring log.
tasks.still_hard: Missing cash transactions and mistaken event assignments require reconciliation.
tasks.human_edge: The writer resolves differences using actual ticket and cash evidence.
tasks.altitude: Less arithmetic and re-keying when a separate manual event log exists.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of gambling services workers
reach.task: Reconcile event cash and settlement records

evidence.claim: Per-event reports and linked workbook formulas can count settled tickets and total payouts without a model; this separate-log scenario is model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is event-level record keeping after ticket transactions. The scenario specifically requires existing manual totals and re-keying into a separate log; already automatic event reporting earns no saving.

The writer's transaction-recording step in task20596, or the cashier's existing payout transaction, produces ticket id, event id, paid amount, status and transaction time during normal settlement. No new capture is transferred to cashiers. Gathering and checking all actual records remains full-time in s1 and s2.
The writer corrects missing or misassigned entries in s2; no ready-made discrepancy flag is assumed. Unresolved transactions stop automatic totals and return to manual reconciliation.

The native report or s3 formulas produce totals from s2's checked set; s4 links those totals into the separate log. These are distinct machine writes with no external send or action commitment; internal saves require no invented self-approval.
Test native reporting before a linked workbook or custom code. Do not introduce a new log merely to automate it.
unknowns: Whether event counts and payouts are already reported automatically
Whether a genuinely separate manual event log exists
research_questions: Can the existing native report replace arithmetic and real re-keying while preserving event reconciliation?

already_counted.description: Record gathering, missing-entry resolution and final log review remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain report filters or workbook links and test rule changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R60, gross40 minus7 upkeep gives net33 for an actual manual event log. Range5-20 assumes only part of arithmetic and separate re-keying remains manual; an already automatic report has zero incremental gain.

tasks.short: Supervise staff and games and mediate disputes

steps.what: Supervise staff and observe game operation
Look up the rule and transaction evidence relevant to a dispute
Mediate the dispute and explain the resolution
Record the dispute facts, resolution and follow-up needs

tasks.design: Index current rules in {DOCS} and configure a contextual dispute form in the {OTHER} wagering system. Supervision and mediation stay human, while rule lookup and repeated record structure become shorter.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the right procedure and writing repetitive incident headings take time around a dispute.
tasks.enabler_now: Native indexed rules and contextual forms can remove navigation and repeated fields.
tasks.still_hard: Accounts conflict and the writer must de-escalate the situation fairly.
tasks.human_edge: The writer understands the people involved and resolves the dispute responsibly.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive lookup and recording; supervisory authority stays the same.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of gambling services workers
reach.learn: Consistent factual records and fair mediation

evidence.claim: Indexed procedures and contextual dispute forms can reduce navigation and repeated record structure; mediation and the proposed time gain are unmeasured model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary includes supervision, evidence lookup, mediation and the actual dispute record. Any payout adjustment is a separate controlled transaction owned by the settlement task, not hidden in mediation.

The writer captures game or ticket id, observed facts, accounts, rule version, resolution and follow-up needs in s4; actual factual capture and review stay counted. No free incident classification or transcript is assumed.
Current house-rule documents are produced by the existing rules owner. Missing rules or uncertain evidence lead to manual clarification; no answer model or automatic decision is used.
Test native rule indexes and contextual forms first. The form touches repeated headings and context only; internal saves earn no saving or self-gate.
unknowns: Share of recording spent on repeated fields rather than facts
research_questions: Does a contextual form shorten records after all factual capture and review are counted?

already_counted.description: Mediation and actual dispute-record capture remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain rule links and incident form context.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100, R91, gross9 minus2 upkeep gives net7. Range1-4 assumes repeated lookup and form fields remain manual; supervision, mediation and factual judgement retain full time.
